passage: "People ask me what it's like sharing a hostel room with Farhan. Honestly? Normal. I'm Sumit. Farhan has tics: his arm jerks, and he says 'yup' a lot, loudly, not because he means yes. First week, I noticed. I didn't say anything. What would I say? We were arguing about whose turn it was to buy milk, and I just kept arguing. When other guys asked 'What's his deal?', I said, 'He's my roommate. He's fine.' About a month in, Farhan brought it up himself, late at night. 'You never asked about the tics.' I said, 'Didn't seem my business. Anything I can do?' He thought, then said, 'Just what you're doing.' Then he beat me at cards."

qa.q: What did Sumit and Farhan argue about in the first week?
qa.a: Whose turn it was to buy milk.

qa.q: What does Farhan saying 'You never asked about the tics' suggest he felt?
qa.a: It suggests he noticed and appreciated that Sumit treated him normally, and felt accepted.

qa.q: Which of Sumit's choices made Farhan feel accepted?
qa.a: Sumit never commented or asked Farhan to stop, carried on normally, and only talked about the tics when Farhan raised them.

qa.q: How might Sumit feel when Farhan says 'Just what you're doing'?
qa.a: Sumit may feel reassured and glad that simply treating Farhan normally was the right thing to do.

grounding: It shows a wise roommate who does not comment on or imitate tics, carries on normally and acknowledges them only when the person raises it.

passage: I'm Ira, and I've worked with Aparna for two years. I learned something from her in a team meeting last week. A new analyst, Kunal, joined us. During his first presentation his shoulder jerked, and he made a quick sniffing sound, again and again. A couple of people glanced at each other. One raised an eyebrow at me. Aparna didn't glance at anyone. She kept her eyes on Kunal's slides and asked, "Can you go back to the chart on sales by region?" as if nothing else was happening. The others followed her lead. Afterwards, by the coffee machine, Kunal said to her, "I have tics, by the way." She said, "Thanks for telling me. Anything you'd like from us?" He said, "No, that was perfect."

qa.q: What did Aparna ask Kunal to go back to?
qa.a: The chart on sales by region.

qa.q: What does Kunal's reply 'that was perfect' suggest about how he felt?
qa.a: It suggests he felt accepted and relieved that the team treated him normally.

qa.q: Which of Aparna's choices set the tone for the team?
qa.a: She kept her eyes on the slides and carried on the discussion, not glancing at anyone, and the others followed.

qa.q: How might the colleague who raised an eyebrow see things after watching Aparna?
qa.a: They might realise that carrying on normally is the respectful response, not exchanging looks.

grounding: A colleague watches a wise coworker who ignores tics respectfully, carries on the conversation and acknowledges them only when the person raises it.
